overview:
Michigan's open Senate seat pits progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed against Republican Mike Rogers to replace retiring Senator Gary Peters. The state is evenly divided at the partisan baseline, but El-Sayed has led in nearly every recent poll, with margins ranging from two to twelve points and a polling average near five. High-quality pollsters including NYT/Siena, AtlasIntel, and YouGov all show him ahead in the final week.

Ratings from nonpartisan analysts cluster between Tilt D and Likely D, and prediction markets price El-Sayed around 77-79%. Rogers benefits from substantial outside support and a well-funded campaign, keeping the race within reach, but the weight of late evidence points to a Democratic hold with a mid-single-digit margin.
